1.stem: The author develops the argument primarily by

options.A: citing field studies of pollination and seed dispersal to settle a long-running dispute
options.B: recounting how eradication campaigns against non-natives rose and then fell out of favor among ecologists
options.C: rejecting the nativist presumption against introduced species in favor of welcoming novel ecosystems
options.D: identifying a shared flaw in two opposing positions and proposing a third criterion for judgment

2.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

options.A: It lays out two rival accounts and presents banding data that favors the second of them.
options.B: It describes a change in migration, attributes it to warmer winters, and notes a complication in the supporting data.
options.C: It sets out two rival accounts, observes that they predict opposite things, and identifies what prevents a test.
options.D: It contrasts the methods of two research teams and argues that one recording scale should be adopted.

3.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

options.A: verbatim transcripts
options.B: provisional drafts
options.C: retrospective compilations
options.D: unofficial abstracts

4.stem: It can most reasonably be inferred that the confident intuitions of a long-range political forecaster

options.A: may feel as certain as an expert nurse's while failing to correspond to reality.
options.B: are unreliable chiefly because forecasters lack adequate training.
options.C: become reliable given a sufficient number of years spent forecasting.
options.D: are felt less strongly than the intuitions of experts in regular environments.

5.stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the interpretation offered in Text 1?

options.A: By agreeing that crows possess a full theory of how automobiles work
options.B: By proposing that the same behavior can arise from learned reward rather than an understanding of cause and effect
options.C: By arguing that the nut-dropping behavior occurs too rarely, and among too few crows, to be worth explaining at all
options.D: By denying that crows actually drop nuts onto roads

6.stem: It can most reasonably be inferred that the author regards the randomized evaluations as

options.A: confirming that the loans raise borrowers' incomes and consumption over the medium term
options.B: showing that microcredit expands business activity without reliably reducing poverty
options.C: too narrow to matter, since they tracked business activity rather than well-being
options.D: proving that borrowing at microcredit rates leaves poor households worse off than before

7.stem: It can most reasonably be inferred that the author regards the flat rotation curves as

options.A: evidence that ultimately favors modified gravity over unseen matter.
options.B: inconsistent with any modification of the gravitational law.
options.C: insufficient on their own to establish the existence of dark matter.
options.D: the strongest single proof that dark matter exists.

8.stem: Which choice is the most reasonable inference from the passage?

options.A: The more frequently a memory is retrieved, the more distorted it grows, since each recall returns the trace to a labile state in which change is inevitable.
options.B: Prediction errors are the only mechanism by which a long-term memory is first formed, so a memory encoded without surprise never stabilizes at all.
options.C: Once a memory has been reconsolidated for the first time, it is permanently fixed and cannot be altered by any later retrieval, however surprising the circumstances.
options.D: A memory recalled in circumstances identical to those in which it was formed is unlikely to be altered by the act of recall.

9.stem: Based on the texts, the author of Text 2 would most likely argue that the remedy proposed in Text 1 is

options.A: misdirected, because seals and smaller predators, not the fleets' sonar and nets, drove the cod population down in the first place
options.B: excessive, because decades of tight limits cost the fishery far more than the cod population ever needed for its recovery
options.C: unnecessary, because the cod were never truly in danger and would have recovered once the fleets moved on to other species
options.D: insufficient, because the ecosystem has changed in ways that limiting the catch cannot reverse

10.stem: What is the main rhetorical function of the final sentence ('The label of irrationality... doing the judging')?

options.A: It concedes that loss-averse behavior is, on balance, irrational after all, despite whatever protection against ruin it happens to offer.
options.B: It relocates the source of the apparent defect from the decision-maker to the framework being used to evaluate the decision.
options.C: It introduces a new experiment designed to test whether cautious choosers really do avoid the ruinous losing streaks described.
options.D: It broadens the argument into the sweeping claim that economic models routinely misjudge every form of human behavior they describe.

11.stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 that a share rule cannot be bargained over in the negotiation that precedes each season's number?

options.A: By denying that a bottom-trawl survey can be conducted often enough to support a quota reset every season.
options.B: By maintaining that a fixed tonnage is easier to enforce at the dock than a share of a survey estimate.
options.C: By accepting that the rule ends the bargaining and adding that it also ends the occasion to question a bad estimate.
options.D: By arguing that fleets' dislike of a variable catch will simply reintroduce the bargaining the rule was meant to end.

12.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the third sentence in the text as a whole?

options.A: It defends the testing protocol by noting that its conditions are held constant across samples.
options.B: It reports the outcome of the most recent germination test on the collection.
options.C: It states the requirement this species' seeds have for a cold interval.
options.D: It introduces the feature of the testing procedure on which the text's doubt turns.

13.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence "The disproportion is deliberate; the failure is the education the successes merely displayed" in the text?

options.A: It criticizes readers who value diplomatic successes over failures.
options.B: It introduces a new failure that the rest of the memoir will examine.
options.C: It explains why the author devoted so much space to a brief, unsuccessful episode.
options.D: It concedes that the negotiation was less important than the author first suggested.

14.stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 that doubling canopy cover produces proportionate declines in heat-related emergency calls?

options.A: By observing that the mortality of new plantings makes the intervention less inexpensive than Text 1 allows.
options.B: By granting that canopy cools but noting that on paved blocks the effect is smaller than two to four degrees.
options.C: By pointing out that the reported declines come from the same programs whose success they are taken to demonstrate.
options.D: By arguing that a citywide canopy total can rise without the trees reaching the blocks where the calls originate.

15.stem: As used in the text, what does the word "color" most nearly mean?

options.A: cause to blush
options.B: apply pigment to
options.C: make more vivid and lively
options.D: bias the impression of

16.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the audience-effect hypothesis described in the passage?

options.A: Cleaners cheat less when bystander fish are visible than when the same client is present with no bystanders in view.
options.B: Cleaners fed a diet richer in parasites bite client mucus less often than cleaners fed a parasite-poor diet.
options.C: Larger client fish are bitten less frequently than smaller ones regardless of whether bystanders are present.
options.D: Clients that have been bitten return to the same cleaner less often than clients that were cleaned honestly.

17.stem: Based on the texts, Anand (Text 2) would most likely characterize the twentieth-century approach described in Text 1 as

options.A: effective for most of the forest, though costly for the few pines whose cones need heat to open.
options.B: counterproductive, since preventing fire can leave certain forests unable to renew themselves and prone to more severe blazes.
options.C: misguided because suppression still failed to keep wildfires from killing the wildlife it was meant to protect.
options.D: reasonable, since extinguishing every blaze quickly spared timber and homes even where a few pine species lost their chance to reseed.

18.stem: Which finding, if true, would most strengthen the revisionists' specific claim as described in the passage?

options.A: Naturalized plants were found to spread more slowly in degraded habitats than in the intact communities that surround them.
options.B: In pristine forests that had never been degraded, introduced plants cut the diversity of native insects by nearly half over two decades of continuous monitoring.
options.C: In sites where native pollinator populations had crashed, animal species persisted only where naturalized plants supplied an alternative food source.
options.D: Across all habitat types, including undamaged ones, ecosystems holding more non-native plants supported a greater total number of animal species than comparable sites.

19.stem: Which finding, if true, would most strengthen the author's argument?

options.A: Surviving records show that transporting grain overland even short distances often cost more than the grain was worth at market.
options.B: Roman engineers produced detailed technical manuals describing how to pave road surfaces durable enough to last for many decades of use.
options.C: Some Roman roads passed through modest towns that later grew into major trading centers of the medieval European economy centuries afterward.
options.D: The Roman navy protected the Mediterranean sea lanes from piracy throughout most of the imperial period.

20.stem: As used in the text, what does the word "economy" most nearly mean? (The blank reads "The economy of the late scores.")

options.A: spareness
options.B: prosperity
options.C: machinery
options.D: frugality

21.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

options.A: accidental
options.B: gradual
options.C: predictable
options.D: reversible

22.stem: Which finding, if true, would most strengthen the author's argument?

options.A: Early printers competed fiercely for the trade in Latin editions of the classical authors.
options.B: In regions that adopted printing early, literacy rose sharply only generations later, once church-led schooling campaigns began.
options.C: Literacy rose fastest in the first decades after the press appeared, well before any schooling campaigns began.
options.D: Across Europe the total number of books in circulation multiplied many times over within a few decades of the first printed editions.

23.stem: A key difference between the two texts is that, unlike the author of Text 1, the author of Text 2

options.A: presents an explanation of galactic rotation that requires no unseen matter, while conceding that it fails at larger scales
options.B: argues that modifying Newton's law at low accelerations accounts for gravitational lensing and the cosmic microwave background as well
options.C: claims that the unseen mass posited by dark-matter models has already been detected directly rather than merely inferred from its gravitational effects
options.D: denies that galaxies rotate faster than the gravity of their own visible matter could ever account for

24.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the last sentence?

options.A: It praises the specialists for confirming the wreck's authenticity.
options.B: It names the general pattern that the specialists' reactions illustrate.
options.C: It introduces a second shipwreck with a conflicting cargo.
options.D: It proposes a revised date for the beginning of regional trade.
